newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.

text.p: Millfeed prices were mostly steady to lower Monday in quiet activity, dealers said.
Some dealers said they believed the market was close to hitting the bottom due to improved demand and reduced feed mill inventories.
"We are dancing around the bottom," a St Louis dealer said. "I see a very limited downside from these levels."

In parts of the upper Midwest, demand has perked up. "I'm finding what I got sold I'd better get shipped, a Minneapolis dealer said. "Demand is good enough to want what's bought. I even had to add a few cars."

But in parts of the Northeast, prices were trending downward. "It is typically a June situation," a Buffalo dealer said. "We have some lower milk prices. We are going to see the dairymen use whatever they can on the farms and stay away from prepared rations as much as they can."
He also noted some flour mills were running six days a week and flour and feed business was still good.
Another dealer noted sluggish demand. "We have beautiful grass," so that would bite into demand," referring to livestock feeding on pasture in the interior like Oklahoma and Kansas.
In the Carolinas, a broker said the flat price of everything was going down. "There are plenty of other ingredients that can also be bought," he said.
"The market is weak." Obviously there is too much nearby supply, a Chattanooga dealer said.
